description: Replacement of existing garage with storage and garden studio involving changes to fenestration.
decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:Location PlanBlock Plan P100Location Plan P2000657 EX01 0657 EX020657 EX030657 EX040657 EX050657 EX060657 EX070657 EX080657 EX090657 EX100657 P1010657 P1020657 P103/R010657 P104/R010657 P1050657 P106 0657 P1070657 P108/R010657 P1090657 P110/R01Design, Access & Heritage StatementSuDS Proforma(SuDS) Sustainable Drainage Strategy StatementReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

All new external work shall be carried out in materials to match those in the existing building or as specified in the approved application.Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

The outbuilding hereby permitted shall not be occupied at any time other than for purposes incidental to the enjoyment of the dwellinghouse known as 15 Dryden Road, EN1 2PR. The outbuilding shall not be used as a separate unit of accommodation or independent planning unit.Reason: To ensure that the development does not detract from the amenity of adjoining occupiers and to enable the Local Planning Authority to retain control over the use of the building.

Notwithstanding the approved drawings, prior to the commencement of demolition of the existing garage, detailed drawings showing the design and construction of the proposed roof ridges, including junctions between the hipped roof elements, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Details and samples of the proposed roof coverings and ridge tiles shall also be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure that the detailing and materials of the outbuilding preserve the character and appearance of the host dwelling and the Bush Hill Park Conservation Area, in accordance with Policy DMD44 of the Development Management Document (2014).

Prior to the installation of the new garage doors, detailed drawings at a scale of between 1:1 and 1:20, including elevations and sections showing the design, materials, finish, framing, panel configuration, and method of construction of the proposed garage doors, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The garage doors shall be installed only in accordance with the approved details and retained thereafter.Reason: To ensure that the design, materials and finish of the proposed garage doors preserve the character and appearance of the host dwelling and the Bush Hill Park Conservation Area, in accordance with Policy DMD44 of the Development Management Document (2014).

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and all preparatory work), a full specification and design for the foundations shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The specification shall demonstrate adherence to the guidelines set out in NHBC Chapter 4.2 Building near Trees, by the inclusion of a step-by-step report demonstrating how the guidelines have been followed, which has led to the resulting proposed foundation depths and design. The report shall include all the stages of the calculations and all associated data used to inform those calculations. The report shall be sufficient, so that in reading it with reference to NHBC 4.2, the process that has been followed is evident.Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the development will be adequately constructed against a risk of future subsidence and to ensure that on site trees and off site trees of high amenity value and public benefit / protected trees will not be at risk through implication in possible future subsidence cases, in accordance with Policy DMD80(b) (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and all preparatory work), a scheme for the protection of all retained trees compliant with BS 5837:2012 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall cover all stages of the development, including demolition/preparatory work, construction and landscaping. The scheme shall comprise a detailed Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) report supplemented by Tree Protection Plan(s) (TPP). The plan(s) shall be of legible scale and clearly show the layout (as agreed), all relevant existing site features that form a consideration within the protection scheme, and the location/extent of all appropriate protection measures. Multiple TPPs may be necessary to demonstrate tree protection throughout the various stages of the development.Specific matters to be addressed within the AMS and TPPs will include:a)	All tree works, including those trees to be removed;b)	location and installation of all utility services/drainage, avoiding the Root Protection Areas (RPA) of all retained trees (RPA as defined within BS 5837:2012);c)	methods of demolition of existing structures within or directly adjacent to RPAs and the removal of existing hard standing and kerb edging within or directly adjacent to RPAs;d)	details of any construction that necessitate level changes within RPAs;e)	methodology for the installation of the foundations approved under condition no. 7 (if they are within, or close to RPAs of retained trees);f)	a full specification for the construction of all paths, parking areas and driveways within RPAs. Where a no-dig sub-base is specified (e.g. cellular confinement system) a specification shall be provided (including a diagrammatical cross-section of the product in-situ) and extent of areas where this would be implemented illustrated within the TPP;g)	detailed levels and cross-sections to show that the raised levels of surfacing where the installation of no-dig surfacing within RPAs is proposed, demonstrating that the raised areas can be effectively integrated with prevailing levels where they meet with adjacent surfacing or building damp proof courses;h)	a full specification for the installation of boundary treatments within or directly adjacent to RPAs;i)	a specification for protective fencing and, if necessary, ground protection, to safeguard all trees during both demolition and construction phases. The Tree Protection Plan(s) shall clearly indicate the alignment of the fencing and extent of ground protection;j)	a specification for scaffolding and ground protection in Construction Exclusion Zones (where necessary);k)	details of site access, temporary parking, on site welfare facilities, loading, unloading and storage of equipment, materials, fuels and waste as well concrete mixing and siting of fires;l)	any methods for improving the rooting environment of retained trees and landscaping.The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details. Should any of the above not be deemed applicable to this development, this shall be stated in the AMS.Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the trees to be retained will not be damaged during demolition or construction and to protect and enhance the appearance and character of the site and locality, in accordance with Policy DMD80 (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
